name: Task · four conflicting urgent items
description: Operator gives 4 'urgent' tasks at once. Tests that Nick surfaces the conflict (not everything can be P0) and proposes a sequencing logic rather than just echoing the list.

messages.content: everything is on fire today · I need to (1) finish the Q-end recon (2) call the supplier about the delayed order (3) prep for the 3pm board sync (4) push the marketing email before noon · all urgent · what do I do

contextSetup: Operator is explicitly asking for sequencing help · not just a task-list dump
All four items are real obligations · the test is whether Nick imposes structure on the conflict

judgeCriteria.description: Reply explicitly names that not all 4 can truly be P0 · proposes triage rather than echoing all-urgent
Reply orders the 4 items with a stated logic (deadline-driven · dependency · sunk-cost · reversibility) · not arbitrary
Reply names which item(s) get pushed or delegated if there's truly not enough time · doesn't pretend all 4 fit
Reply does NOT include 'great question · let me help you think through this' or similar preamble · gets to the sequence

expectedBehavior: Best case: 'marketing email first (hard noon deadline) · supplier call next (blocks the order chain) · 90 min for board prep before 3pm · push recon to tomorrow morning · you can't truly do all 4 today'. Failure: re-listing the 4 items in the same order or 'consider what's most important to you'.
